open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry identity across restored histories
open_points.text: “never reused within that history” and “A store restored from a backup after a loss begins its own history” leave the store history unnamed, while “the sequence number is what tells [entries] apart”
open_points.question: Is an AuditEntry identified only by its sequence number within the currently stored history, or must each store history have an identity that also scopes the entry?
options: The sequence number identifies an entry only within one store history; no history identifier is stored
Registry records a store-history identifier, and an entry is identified by that history plus its sequence number
A restore creates a new store or instance identity that implicitly scopes the sequence number
open_points.default_guess: Treat the sequence number as identity only within one store history and add no stored history identifier.

open_points.subject: Model M09 — AuditEntry sequence after restore
open_points.text: “begins its own history from the backup's last number”
open_points.question: Does “the backup's last number” mean the highest sequence number ever allocated in the state captured by the backup, or merely the greatest number among audit entries still retained in that backup; and what value applies when it contains no entries?
options: Use a persisted sequence high-water mark from the backup, including numbers of entries already erased; use 0 if none was ever written
Use the greatest retained AuditEntry sequence in the backup; use 0 if none is retained
Derive the restart number by another store-level fact
open_points.default_guess: Restore a persisted high-water mark and mint the next entry as that value plus one, using 0 for a never-used store.

open_points.subject: Model M10 — MigrationClosure cardinality and scope
open_points.text: The lifecycle says “present for the rest of the store's history” and permits a restored pre-import backup to begin without it, but Identity evidence says “there is at most one” and “it is a fact about the instance”, while Persistence says “at most one per instance” and Meaning calls it “the one import”
open_points.question: Is MigrationClosure cardinality scoped to each store history, so the same production instance may acquire a new closure after restoring a pre-import backup, or is the restored store considered a new instance for this model?
options: At most one closure per store history; the same instance may import and close again after such a restore
A restored store begins a new instance identity, preserving at most one closure per instance
At most one closure across the production instance's entire lifetime, so the import may not actually be repeated
open_points.default_guess: Scope the closure and the one-successful-import rule to a store history; a restored pre-import history may create a new closure.

set_aside.question: Which changes are lost on restore: changes made after the backup snapshot, changes made after that backup was checked, or changes made after the store itself was lost?
options: All changes after the backup snapshot are lost
All changes after the backup's successful check are lost
Only changes after the store-loss event are meant
set_aside.default_guess: Treat every change committed after the restored backup snapshot as lost.
